blocks.content: The Competition Commission of India is established to eliminate practices having adverse effect on competition, promote and sustain competition, protect the interests of consumers and ensure freedom of trade in India.

rows: Control of monopolies and curbing concentration of economic power
Promoting open market competition and consumer interest
Based on firm size and total asset value
Based on market conduct and anti-competitive behavior
No explicit provision for heavy financial penalties
Can impose fines up to 10% of the average turnover

items: Appeals against orders passed by the CCI lie with the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT).
Members of the CCI hold office for a term of 5 years or until reaching 65 years of age, whichever comes earlier.
The Selection Committee for CCI appointments is headed by the Chief Justice of India or a nominee CJI judge.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) was established under the Competition Act, 2002 to foster a healthy, competitive market environment.
It officially replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Commission (MRTPC) following the recommendations of the SV Raghavan Committee.
The Commission comprises a Chairperson and not less than two and not more than six Members appointed by the Central Government.
Key mandates include preventing anti-competitive agreements, curbing the abuse of dominant market position, and regulating mergers and acquisitions (combinations).
